company.name: Living Carbon
company.shortDescription: Living Carbon is a public benefit company on a mission to fight climate change by genetically enhancing CO2 capture and storage in trees.
company.description: The goal of the public benefit corporation Living Carbon is to restore equilibrium to the planet's metabolic process. We address this urgency by fusing cutting-edge biotechnology with plants' natural ability to capture and store carbon. Living Carbon is a public benefit corporation with the goal of rebalancing the planet's metabolic system. In order to fulfill this need, tey combine cutting-edge biotechnology with plants' natural ability to capture and store carbon. The company was established in 2019 by Maddie Hall and Patrick Mellor in San Francisco, California.

productsAndServices.description: A program that partners with landowners to restore degraded or abandoned lands through reforestation, providing free seedlings, site preparation, planting, and annual payments while retaining land ownership and access.

productsAndServices.description: Development and sale of carbon removal credits generated from reforestation projects on degraded lands, aimed at corporations seeking to offset emissions.

productsAndServices.description: Development of fast-growing hybrid poplar trees tailored to accumulate more biomass, offered as custom biomass feedstocks near processing facilities or supply chains.

aiResearchSummary.text: Living Carbon is researching and developing compositions and methods for enhancing biomass productivity in plants, as described in their work on transgenic plant cells containing polynucleotide sequences encoding glycolate dehydrogenase, malate synthase, and an inhibitory polynucleotide targeting an endogenous glycolate transporter. These efforts focus on genetically enhancing CO2 capture and storage in trees, aligning with their mission to address climate change.

insights.title: Funding is concentrated in the latest major round

caveats: Only rounds with a disclosed post-money valuation are compared.
